text:
The parse error comes from the model name. The allowed element types are `nfet` and `pfet`, so `nfet_01v8_lvt` is rejected. I've switched M2 to `nfet`, which removes the LVT threshold reduction the old sizing relied on. To compensate, I widened M2 from 22 to 42 so the load still sets an output level near 0.9 V with about 0.47 mA of current. That gives a load resistance of roughly 0.5 kΩ, which supports the 590 MHz bandwidth at 500 fF.

These are first-order hand estimates (about 3 dB gain, roughly 670 MHz f-3dB, roughly 950 MHz GBW, under 1 mW). I have not run the simulator, so please verify across corners and temperatures before relying on them.

```spice
.subckt dut vin vout vdd vss ibias
* Reference: diode-connected NMOS sinks IREF from ibias (unchanged)
Mref ibias ibias vss vss nfet W=2 L=0.5
* 1:1 mirror sink of ~20 uA from vout (unchanged)
M3   vout  ibias vss vss nfet W=2 L=0.5
* Input common-source transistor (unchanged, sinks ~0.45 mA at Vgs=0.75 V)
M1   vout  vin   vss vss nfet W=90 L=0.5
* Load: NMOS source follower with gate and drain at VDD, source at vout.
* Acts as a ~0.5 kOhm pull-up that sets vout near 0.9 V.
* Changed from nfet_01v8_lvt (not an allowed model) to nfet; W raised 22 -> 42
* to compensate for the higher threshold and keep the load current near 0.47 mA.
M2   vdd   vdd   vout vss nfet W=42 L=0.5
.ends dut
```
